tags:
  - attack.credential_access
  - attack.discovery
  - attack.t1552.001
  - attack.t1083
  - attack.t1057
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_image:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
      - '/dash'
      - '/zsh'
      - '/cat'
      - '/grep'
      - '/awk'
      - '/find'
      - '/xargs'
      - '/tr'
      - '/strings'
  selection_cmd:
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '/proc/'
      - '/environ'
  condition: selection_image and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
  - Forensic / DFIR triage tooling intentionally enumerating process environments
  - Performance diagnostics scripts inspecting a single PID's environ (lower /proc cardinality)
level: high
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE (@process.command_line:*/proc/*/environ* OR @process.executable.path:(/usr/bin/cat OR /bin/cat OR /usr/bin/grep OR /usr/bin/awk OR /usr/bin/find OR /usr/bin/xargs OR /usr/bin/strings)) AND @process.command_line:*environ*
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 CommandLine=/\/proc\/[^\s\/]+\/environ/
| ImageFileName=/(bash|sh|dash|zsh|cat|grep|awk|find|xargs|tr|strings|head|tail)$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, ParentBaseFileName, CommandLine, UserName], function=count())
| count > 0
CLOUD
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process="*/proc/*" Processes.process="*/environ*" (Processes.process_name=bash OR Processes.process_name=sh OR Processes.process_name=dash OR Processes.process_name=zsh OR Processes.process_name=cat OR Processes.process_name=grep OR Processes.process_name=awk OR Processes.process_name=find OR Processes.process_name=xargs OR Processes.process_name=tr OR Processes.process_name=strings) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process="*/proc/*" Processes.process="*/environ*" (Processes.process_name=bash OR Processes.process_name=sh OR Processes.process_name=dash OR Processes.process_name=zsh OR Processes.process_name=cat OR Processes.process_name=grep OR Processes.process_name=awk OR Processes.process_name=find OR Processes.process_name=xargs OR Processes.process_name=tr OR Processes.process_name=strings) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("216.126.225.129") or RemoteUrl has_any ("polymarketbot.polymarketdev.workers.dev")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic(["216.126.225.129"]);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["polymarketbot.polymarketdev.workers.dev"]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr in (BadIPs)
   or Url has_any (BadDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkProtocol
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Outbound Connection to Article-Named IP / Domain
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0f
status: experimental
description: |
    Replace `__IP_LIST__` / `__DOMAIN_LIST__` placeholders with
    article-specific destinations. For dynamic IOC management, use a
    watchlist or external feed.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/tactics/TA0011/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.command-and-control
logsource:
    category: network_connection
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_ip:
        DestinationIp:
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_2__'
    selection_domain:
        DestinationHostname:
            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_2__'
    condition: selection_ip or selection_domain
falsepositives:
    - None on a true-positive IOC match
level: critical
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.dest IN ("216.126.225.129")
    by All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest, All_Traffic.dest_port
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Web
        where Web.dest IN ("polymarketbot.polymarketdev.workers.dev")
        by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`]
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
        where DNS.query IN ("polymarketbot.polymarketdev.workers.dev")
        by DNS.src, DNS.query, DNS.answer
     | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`]
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.dest IN ("216.126.225.129")
    by All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest, All_Traffic.dest_port
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| append
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Web
        where Web.dest IN ("polymarketbot.polymarketdev.workers.dev")
        by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`]
| append
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
        where DNS.query IN ("polymarketbot.polymarketdev.workers.dev")
        by DNS.src, DNS.query, DNS.answer
     | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`]
Suspicious browser extension installation Installation Medium
Side-loaded / unsigned extensions, often masquerading as wallets, productivity tools.
ATT&CKT1176
Data sourcesEndpoint.Registry DeviceRegistryEvents
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where RegistryKey has_any ("\Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\","\Software\Microsoft\Edge\Extensions\","\Software\Mozilla\Firefox\Extensions\")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RegistryKey, RegistryValueName, RegistryValueData,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName
ImRegistryEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where RegistryKey has_any (@"\Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\",
                              @"\Software\Microsoft\Edge\Extensions\",
                              @"\Software\Mozilla\Firefox\Extensions\")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, RegistryKey,
          RegistryValue, RegistryValueData, ActingProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Browser Extension Installation via Registry
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0a
status: experimental
description: |
    Registry writes under the browser extension policy keys —
    administrative install of an extension. Often used by adware /
    info-stealers to bypass user-level extension controls.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1176/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1176
    - attack.persistence
logsource:
    category: registry_event
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        TargetObject|contains:
            - '\Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\'
            - '\Software\Microsoft\Edge\Extensions\'
            - '\Software\Mozilla\Firefox\Extensions\'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Group-policy-managed extension whitelists
level: medium
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry
    where (Registry.registry_path="*\Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\*"
        OR Registry.registry_path="*\Software\Microsoft\Edge\Extensions\*"
        OR Registry.registry_path="*\Software\Mozilla\Firefox\Extensions\*")
    by Registry.dest, Registry.registry_path, Registry.registry_value_data, Registry.registry_value_name, Registry.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry
    where (Registry.registry_path="*\Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\*"
        OR Registry.registry_path="*\Software\Microsoft\Edge\Extensions\*"
        OR Registry.registry_path="*\Software\Mozilla\Firefox\Extensions\*")
    by Registry.dest, Registry.registry_path, Registry.registry_value_data, Registry.registry_value_name, Registry.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)`
Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Crypto-wallet file/keystore access by non-wallet process Actions on Objectives High
Stealers / wallet drainers read keystore.json, MetaMask, Exodus, Atomic, Phantom data.
ATT&CKT1005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Ethereum\keystore\", @"\Bitcoin\", @"\Exodus\", @"\Electrum\wallets\", @"\MetaMask\", @"\Phantom\", @"\Atomic\Local Storage\")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MetaMask.exe","Exodus.exe","Atomic.exe","electrum.exe","Bitcoin.exe","Phantom.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Ethereum\keystore\", @"\Bitcoin\",
                                  @"\Exodus\", @"\Electrum\wallets\",
                                  @"\MetaMask\", @"\Phantom\",
                                  @"\Atomic\Local Storage\")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("MetaMask.exe","Exodus.exe","Atomic.exe",
                                  "electrum.exe","Bitcoin.exe","Phantom.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Crypto-Wallet Keystore Access by Non-Wallet Process
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d02
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers / wallet drainers read keystore files from MetaMask,
    Exodus, Atomic, Phantom, Bitcoin, Electrum, Ethereum-cli wallets.
    Filtering out the legitimate wallet binaries leaves only attacker
    activity.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1005/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1005
    - attack.collection
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Ethereum\keystore\'
            - '\Bitcoin\'
            - '\Exodus\'
            - '\Electrum\wallets\'
            - '\MetaMask\'
            - '\Phantom\'
            - '\Atomic\Local Storage\'
    filter_legit:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\MetaMask.exe'
            - '\Exodus.exe'
            - '\Atomic.exe'
            - '\electrum.exe'
            - '\Bitcoin.exe'
            - '\Phantom.exe'
    condition: selection_path and not filter_legit
falsepositives:
    - Backup software
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Ethereum\keystore\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Bitcoin\wallet.dat"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Exodus\exodus.wallet*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Electrum\wallets\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\MetaMask\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Phantom\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Atomic\Local Storage\*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("MetaMask.exe","Exodus.exe","Atomic.exe","electrum.exe","Bitcoin.exe","Phantom.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Ethereum\keystore\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Bitcoin\wallet.dat"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Exodus\exodus.wallet*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Electrum\wallets\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\MetaMask\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Phantom\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Atomic\Local Storage\*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("MetaMask.exe","Exodus.exe","Atomic.exe","electrum.exe","Bitcoin.exe","Phantom.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: LSASS Process Access Outside Microsoft-Signed Tooling
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d04
status: experimental
description: |
    Anything opening lsass.exe with read-memory access that isn't a
    Microsoft signed component (Defender, csrss, etc.) is suspect.
    Mimikatz / Pypykatz / nanodump signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1003.001
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: process_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        TargetImage|endswith: '\lsass.exe'
    filter_known_good:
        SourceImage|endswith:
            - '\MsSense.exe'
            - '\MsMpEng.exe'
            - '\csrss.exe'
            - '\svchost.exe'
            - '\wininit.exe'
            - '\services.exe'
            - '\lsm.exe'
            - '\SearchProtocolHost.exe'
    condition: selection and not filter_known_good
falsepositives:
    - Third-party EDR / forensic tools — extend the filter list
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("e01b85c1437085a519217338fe4ee5ed7858c28a10f8c1477b2f1857c3386edb", "acac5a9854650c4ae2883c4740bf87d34120c038") or SHA1 in~ ("e01b85c1437085a519217338fe4ee5ed7858c28a10f8c1477b2f1857c3386edb", "acac5a9854650c4ae2883c4740bf87d34120c038") or MD5 in~ ("e01b85c1437085a519217338fe4ee5ed7858c28a10f8c1477b2f1857c3386edb", "acac5a9854650c4ae2883c4740bf87d34120c038")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("e01b85c1437085a519217338fe4ee5ed7858c28a10f8c1477b2f1857c3386edb", "acac5a9854650c4ae2883c4740bf87d34120c038") or SHA1 in~ ("e01b85c1437085a519217338fe4ee5ed7858c28a10f8c1477b2f1857c3386edb", "acac5a9854650c4ae2883c4740bf87d34120c038") or MD5 in~ ("e01b85c1437085a519217338fe4ee5ed7858c28a10f8c1477b2f1857c3386edb", "acac5a9854650c4ae2883c4740bf87d34120c038")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["e01b85c1437085a519217338fe4ee5ed7858c28a10f8c1477b2f1857c3386edb", "acac5a9854650c4ae2883c4740bf87d34120c038"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Making Vulnerable Drivers Exploitable Without Hardware - The BYOVD Perspective

The Hacker News
2026-05-22 8 use cases 4 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

1 Introduction This article provides a technical analysis of how many Windows kernel mode drivers can be interacted with from user mode without the hardware they were developed for. This work was motivated by driver-oriented vulnerability research and the need to evaluate the exploitability of individual findings, which frequently affect code whose reachability is hardware-gated. [LLM] BYOVD kernel-driver service deployment via sc.exe create + start correlation Installation High
Detects the exact two-step BYOVD deployment sequence the article calls out: `sc.exe create <name> type= kernel start= demand binPath= System32\drivers\<x>.sys` followed by `sc.exe start <name>` on the same host. Sharpens the canonical SigmaHQ kernel-driver rule by requiring the start-follow-up + a .sys binPath ending, eliminating sysadmin driver-install noise. Rationale: Anchored on the article's literal deployment command (`sc.exe create ... type= kernel start= demand binPath= System32\drivers\<x>.sys` + `sc.exe start <name>`). The temporal correlation between create+start within 10min on the same service name is what differentiates BYOVD operator behaviour from a sysadmin reading docs. Cross-checked SigmaHQ `proc_creation_win_sc_new_kernel_driver.yml` and confirmed the canonical rule does NOT correlate the start follow-up — that's the value-add here. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/SigmaHQ/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/proc_creation_win_sc_new_kernel_driver.yml • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1068/ • https://www.crowdstrike.com/en-us/blog/scattered-spider-attempts-to-avoid-detection-with-bring-your-own-vulnerable-driver-tactic/ • https://www.picussecurity.com/resource/blog/what-are-bring-your-own-vulnerable-driver-byovd-attacks
ATT&CKT1068 T1562.001 T1543.003

    | project CreateTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, AccountName, CreateCmd = ProcessCommandLine, ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFileName, SvcName;
let Starts = DeviceProcessEvents

[LLM] Kernel-type service registry creation with .sys ImagePath by user-context process Installation Medium
Detects the registry artefact of any BYOVD service install — a new value under `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\<name>\` where `Type=0x1` (kernel driver) and `ImagePath` references a .sys outside the protected DriverStore. Catches BYOVD frameworks that bypass sc.exe and write the registry directly (CreateServiceW / advapi32). Rationale: Article §3.1 names the registry-and-service install pattern (`sc.exe create ... type= kernel ... binPath= System32\drivers\X.sys`) as the BYOVD prerequisite, and the registry artefact persists even when attackers skip sc.exe entirely (calling CreateServiceW directly). Sysmon EID 13 captures both `Type` and `ImagePath` writes; pairing them on the same service name + filtering DriverStore + TrustedInstaller eliminates Windows Update / OEM driver noise. Cross-checked against CrowdStrike's Scattered Spider BYOVD writeup which lists the same registry hive as the canonical pivot. Cross-checked against: • https://www.crowdstrike.com/en-us/blog/scattered-spider-attempts-to-avoid-detection-with-bring-your-own-vulnerable-driver-tactic/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1543/003/ • https://www.splunk.com/en_us/blog/security/these-are-the-drivers-you-are-looking-for-detect-and-prevent-malicious-drivers.html
ATT&CKT1543.003 T1068
Data sourcesEndpoint.Registry
let TypeWrites = DeviceRegistryEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where ActionType in ("RegistryValueSet","RegistryKeyCreated")
    | where RegistryKey matches regex @"(?i)\\SYSTEM\\(CurrentControlSet|ControlSet00\d)\\Services\\[^\\]+$"
    | where RegistryValueName =~ "Type"
    | where RegistryValueData in ("1","0x1","0x00000001")
    | extend SvcName = tostring(split(RegistryKey, "\\")[-1])
    | project TypeTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, SvcName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine;
let ImageWrites = DeviceRegistryEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where ActionType in ("RegistryValueSet","RegistryKeyCreated")
    | where RegistryKey matches regex @"(?i)\\SYSTEM\\(CurrentControlSet|ControlSet00\d)\\Services\\[^\\]+$"
    | where RegistryValueName =~ "ImagePath"
    | where RegistryValueData has ".sys"
    | where RegistryValueData !contains "\\DriverStore\\"
    | extend SvcName = tostring(split(RegistryKey, "\\")[-1])
    | project ImageTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, SvcName, ImagePath = RegistryValueData;
TypeWrites
| join kind=inner ImageWrites on DeviceId, SvcName
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("TrustedInstaller.exe","msiexec.exe","services.exe","setup.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| project TypeTime, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, SvcName, ImagePath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by TypeTime desc
Event
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Source == "Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon" and EventID == 13
| extend ed = parse_xml(EventData)
| extend TargetObject = tostring(ed.DataItem.EventData.Data[3].["#text"])
| extend Details = tostring(ed.DataItem.EventData.Data[4].["#text"])
| extend ImageProc = tostring(ed.DataItem.EventData.Data[5].["#text"])
| where TargetObject matches regex @"(?i)\\SYSTEM\\(CurrentControlSet|ControlSet00\d)\\Services\\[^\\]+\\(Type|ImagePath)$"
| extend SvcName = extract(@"(?i)\\Services\\([^\\]+)\\", 1, TargetObject)
| extend Field = extract(@"(?i)\\([^\\]+)$", 1, TargetObject)
| summarize TypeVal = anyif(Details, Field =~ "Type"), ImageVal = anyif(Details, Field =~ "ImagePath"), Proc = any(ImageProc), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated) by Computer, SvcName
| where TypeVal in ("1","0x1","DWORD (0x00000001)") and ImageVal has ".sys"
| where ImageVal !contains "\\DriverStore\\"
| where Proc !endswith "\\TrustedInstaller.exe" and Proc !endswith "\\msiexec.exe" and Proc !endswith "\\services.exe"
| project FirstSeen, Computer, SvcName, ImageVal, Proc
| order by FirstSeen desc
title: New Kernel-Type Service Registered with Non-DriverStore .sys ImagePath
id: 8f3c7d22-ba1e-4e7e-9a45-3f7b1d4f9d22
status: experimental
description: Detects creation of a Windows service registry key with Type=0x1 (kernel driver) whose ImagePath references a .sys file outside the protected DriverStore. Used by BYOVD frameworks that drop a vulnerable driver and register it as a kernel service for IRP reachability.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/making-vulnerable-drivers-exploitable.html
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1068/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1543/003/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/23
tags:
  - attack.t1068
  - attack.t1543.003
  - attack.t1562.001
  - attack.defense_evasion
  - attack.privilege_escalation
logsource:
  category: registry_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_type:
    TargetObject|re: '(?i)\\SYSTEM\\(CurrentControlSet|ControlSet00\d)\\Services\\[^\\]+\\Type$'
    Details:
      - 'DWORD (0x00000001)'
      - '0x00000001'
      - '0x1'
      - '1'
  filter_trusted:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\TrustedInstaller.exe'
      - '\msiexec.exe'
      - '\services.exe'
  condition: selection_type and not filter_trusted
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate signed third-party driver installation (printer, GPU, VPN, AV)
  - Endpoint management tooling (SCCM/Intune) deploying drivers via custom scripts
level: medium
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:13 @TargetObject:(*\\Services\\*\\Type OR *\\Services\\*\\ImagePath OR *\\services\\*\\type OR *\\services\\*\\imagepath) -@Image:(*\\TrustedInstaller.exe OR *\\trustedinstaller.exe OR *\\msiexec.exe OR *\\MSIEXEC.exe OR *\\services.exe)
#event_simpleName=AsepValueUpdate RegObjectName=/\\Services\\[^\\]+$/i (RegValueName=/^Type$/i OR RegValueName=/^ImagePath$/i)
| case {
    RegValueName=/^Type$/i RegStringValue=/^(1|0x0*1)$/ | KernelType:="true";
    RegValueName=/^ImagePath$/i RegStringValue=/\.sys/i NOT RegStringValue=/\\DriverStore\\/i | HasDriverPath:="true";
  }
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, RegObjectName], function={ collect([RegValueName, RegStringValue, ContextImageFileName, KernelType, HasDriverPath]) })
| KernelType="true" HasDriverPath="true"
| NOT ContextImageFileName=/\\(TrustedInstaller|msiexec|services)\.exe$/i
ENDPOINT

| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Registry.registry_value_data) as value_data values(Registry.process_path) as proc_path from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry where Registry.registry_path="*\\System\\CurrentControlSet\\Services\\*\\Type" Registry.registry_value_data="0x00000001" by Registry.dest Registry.user Registry.registry_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)` | rex field=registry_path "Services\\\\(?<svc_name>[^\\\\]+)\\\\Type" | join type=inner svc_name [| tstats `summariesonly` values(Registry.registry_value_data) as image_path from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry where Registry.registry_path="*\\System\\CurrentControlSet\\Services\\*\\ImagePath" by Registry.registry_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)` | rex field=registry_path "Services\\\\(?<svc_name>[^\\\\]+)\\\\ImagePath"] | where like(image_path,"%.sys%") AND NOT like(image_path,"%\\DriverStore\\%") AND NOT like(proc_path,"%\\TrustedInstaller.exe") AND NOT like(proc_path,"%\\msiexec.exe") | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | table firstTime, dest, user, svc_name, image_path, proc_path
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Registry.registry_value_data) as value_data values(Registry.process_path) as proc_path from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry where Registry.registry_path="*\\System\\CurrentControlSet\\Services\\*\\Type" Registry.registry_value_data="0x00000001" by Registry.dest Registry.user Registry.registry_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)` | rex field=registry_path "Services\\\\(?<svc_name>[^\\\\]+)\\\\Type" | join type=inner svc_name [| tstats summariesonly=false values(Registry.registry_value_data) as image_path from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry where Registry.registry_path="*\\System\\CurrentControlSet\\Services\\*\\ImagePath" by Registry.registry_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)` | rex field=registry_path "Services\\\\(?<svc_name>[^\\\\]+)\\\\ImagePath"] | where like(image_path,"%.sys%") AND NOT like(image_path,"%\\DriverStore\\%") AND NOT like(proc_path,"%\\TrustedInstaller.exe") AND NOT like(proc_path,"%\\msiexec.exe") | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | table firstTime, dest, user, svc_name, image_path, proc_path
[LLM] Driver .sys dropped to System32\drivers by user-context process Delivery Medium
Detects the BYOVD file-staging step: a .sys file written into `C:\Windows\System32\drivers\` (the canonical binPath target in the article's deployment command) by a process that is not TrustedInstaller, msiexec, Windows Update or the DriverStore. Pre-stages the alert before the sc.exe service-create fires, giving SOC a chance to catch the drop pre-load. Rationale: Article §3.1 deployment command names `System32\drivers\<x>.sys` as the binPath target. Any .sys landing there from a non-installer process is the pre-load BYOVD staging step. SHA256 from this hit feeds straight into a loldrivers.io / Microsoft Vulnerable Driver Blocklist lookup. Filtering DriverStore/WinSxS/TrustedInstaller is what makes this rule production-viable rather than dashboard noise — confirmed against Splunk's published guidance on driver-write monitoring. Cross-checked against: • https://www.splunk.com/en_us/blog/security/these-are-the-drivers-you-are-looking-for-detect-and-prevent-malicious-drivers.html • https://reversingops.com/posts/detecting-driver-loading-techniques/ • https://loldrivers.io/
ATT&CKT1068 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed")
| where FolderPath matches regex @"(?i)\\Windows\\System32\\drivers\\?$"
| where FileName endswith ".sys"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("TrustedInstaller.exe","msiexec.exe","drvinst.exe","wuauclt.exe","MoUsoCoreWorker.exe","setup.exe","DismHost.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith "C:\\Windows\\WinSxS\\"
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith "C:\\Windows\\System32\\DriverStore\\"
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !in~ ("system","local service","network service")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, SHA256, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed")
| where TargetFilePath matches regex @"(?i)\\Windows\\System32\\drivers\\[^\\]+\.sys$"
| where ActingProcessName !endswith "\\TrustedInstaller.exe"
  and ActingProcessName !endswith "\\msiexec.exe"
  and ActingProcessName !endswith "\\drvinst.exe"
  and ActingProcessName !endswith "\\wuauclt.exe"
  and ActingProcessName !endswith "\\DismHost.exe"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine !contains "\\DriverStore\\"
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$" and ActorUsername !in~ ("SYSTEM","LOCAL SERVICE","NETWORK SERVICE")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256, TargetFilePath, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Driver File Dropped to System32 Drivers Directory by User Context
id: 1b2e9c44-7c84-4ad1-a3e8-04a0fbc63bea
status: experimental
description: Detects creation of a .sys file in C:\Windows\System32\drivers by a process that is not TrustedInstaller, msiexec, drvinst, or the Windows Update stack. Article-anchored on the BYOVD deployment target path documented by Atos research.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/making-vulnerable-drivers-exploitable.html
  - https://loldrivers.io/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/23
tags:
  - attack.t1068
  - attack.t1105
  - attack.defense_evasion
  - attack.privilege_escalation
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|re: '(?i)\\Windows\\System32\\drivers\\[^\\]+\.sys$'
  filter_installers:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\TrustedInstaller.exe'
      - '\msiexec.exe'
      - '\drvinst.exe'
      - '\wuauclt.exe'
      - '\DismHost.exe'

falsepositives:

  - In-place Windows feature upgrade staging
level: medium
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 @TargetFilename:(*\\System32\\drivers\\*.sys OR *\\system32\\drivers\\*.sys OR *\\SYSTEM32\\DRIVERS\\*.sys) -@Image:(*\\TrustedInstaller.exe OR *\\trustedinstaller.exe OR *\\msiexec.exe OR *\\drvinst.exe OR *\\DrvInst.exe OR *\\wuauclt.exe OR *\\DismHost.exe OR *\\MoUsoCoreWorker.exe)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten TargetFileName=/\\Windows\\System32\\drivers\\[^\\]+\.sys$/i
| NOT ContextImageFileName=/\\(TrustedInstaller|msiexec|drvinst|wuauclt|DismHost|MoUsoCoreWorker)\.exe$/i
| NOT ContextImageFileName=/\\System32\\DriverStore\\/i
| NOT ContextImageFileName=/\\Windows\\WinSxS\\/i

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT

    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files

    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem

LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] UTA0355 device-code phishing: deviceCode auth flow with cross-IP token redemption · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender

Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] ROADtools roadtx FOCI client-ID swap: refresh-token resource hop across MS Office FOCI app IDs

[LLM] Curious Serpens / APT29 ROADtools-pattern: device registration immediately following non-interactive token acquisition Installation Medium
Hunts for the ROADtools roadtx device-registration sequence where an Entra ID device is registered (T1098.005) shortly after a non-interactive token grant — the pattern Microsoft attributed to Midnight Blizzard / Curious Serpens. Catches attacker-controlled devices being joined as a persistence foothold after token theft. Rationale: Article ties Cloaked Ursa/APT29 and Curious Serpens to ROADtools device-registration persistence (T1098.005). The roadtx module registers devices using one of the public FOCI client IDs (Azure CLI 04b07795, Azure PowerShell 1b730954, Microsoft Office d3590ed6) via non-interactive token flows — joining that to the Audit-Log device add within 30 minutes from a different IP catches the attacker-device persistence pattern. Cross-checked Microsoft Threat Intel reporting on Midnight Blizzard ROADtools usage. Cross-checked against: • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2022/08/24/magicweb-nobeliums-post-compromise-trick-to-authenticate-as-anyone/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1098/005/ • https://www.volexity.com/blog/2025/04/22/phishing-for-codes-russian-threat-actors-target-microsoft-365-oauth-workflows/

[LLM] UTA0355 device-code phishing: deviceCode auth flow with cross-IP token redemption Delivery High
Hunts for the UTA0355 (Volexity, 2025) targeted phishing TTP where a victim is sent a device-code prompt and the resulting token is redeemed from attacker infrastructure. ROADtools' roadtx module supports the device_code flow natively; the cross-IP redemption (different IP between code issuance and token use) is the high-fidelity signal. Rationale: Article explicitly cites Volexity's UTA0355 device-code phishing campaign and notes roadtx's device_code flow support. Device-code authentication is rare in normal user populations and a multi-IP redemption inside a 15-minute window is a near-textbook indicator of phished-code abuse — Volexity called this exact pattern out as the UTA0355 IoC. Cross-checked Volexity's April 2025 report. Cross-checked against: • https://www.volexity.com/blog/2025/04/22/phishing-for-codes-russian-threat-actors-target-microsoft-365-oauth-workflows/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1528/ • https://github.com/dirkjanm/ROADtools
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1528 T1550.001

[LLM] ROADtools roadtx FOCI client-ID swap: refresh-token resource hop across MS Office FOCI app IDs Command & Control Medium
Hunts for roadtx's signature behaviour of exchanging a refresh token issued to one Microsoft Family of Client IDs (FOCI) app for an access token on a different FOCI app — a defense-evasion trick to broaden token scope without re-prompting MFA. Detection identifies the same refresh-token correlation hitting multiple FOCI app IDs within a short window. Rationale: Article describes roadtx exploiting OAuth on-behalf-of and refresh-token reuse to enable persistence and broaden access; this matches the publicly-documented FOCI refresh-token hopping behaviour (Secureworks, Microsoft research). Detecting >=3 distinct FOCI client IDs sharing refresh-token continuity in <10 minutes for one UPN is high-fidelity for roadtx token replay. Cross-checked Secureworks FOCI research and dirkjanm/ROADtools GitHub. Cross-checked against: • https://www.secureworks.com/research/family-of-client-ids • https://github.com/dirkjanm/ROADtools • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1550/001/

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web

     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time

| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count

          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime

    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process

| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`

status: experimental
description: |

        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"

[LLM] PowerShell-parented taskkill of winrar.exe (Cloud Atlas LNK anti-forensic cleanup) Installation High
Hunts the Step 6 'process concealment' action in the Fixed.ps1 loader chain - PowerShell spawning taskkill.exe /F /IM winrar.exe immediately after the LNK-launched stager extracts the decoy PDF. This pairing is highly article-specific and uncommon outside attacker cleanup routines. Rationale: Anchored on the exact Step 6 string from the article's Fixed.ps1 action table: 'taskkill.exe /F /Im winrar.exe' with PowerShell as parent. Cross-checked Cloud Atlas (aka Inception) on MITRE ATT&CK G0100 confirms loader pattern. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0100/ • https://securelist.com/cloud-atlas/68083/
ATT&CKT1070.004 T1562.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName =~ "taskkill.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "winrar.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/F", "/IM")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "powershell.exe"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\taskkill.exe"
| where CommandLine contains "winrar.exe"
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\\powershell.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
title: PowerShell spawning taskkill against winrar.exe (Cloud Atlas anti-forensic)
id: 8a3e3c9c-1d5f-4d1a-9e9b-1c0c8c4a7e11
description: Detects PowerShell parent process spawning taskkill.exe targeting winrar.exe - Cloud Atlas Fixed.ps1 loader cleanup step 6.
references:
  - https://securelist.com/cloud-atlas-2026/119895/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/23
tags:
  - attack.t1070.004
  - attack.t1562.001
  - attack.defense_evasion
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_img:
    Image|endswith: '\taskkill.exe'
    ParentImage|endswith: '\powershell.exe'
  selection_cmd:
    CommandLine|contains: 'winrar.exe'
  selection_flags:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '/F'
      - '/IM'
  condition: selection_img and selection_cmd and selection_flags
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @Image:(*\\taskkill.exe OR *\\TASKKILL.EXE) @CommandLine:(*winrar.exe* OR *WinRAR.exe* OR *WINRAR.EXE*) @ParentImage:(*\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\POWERSHELL.EXE)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\\taskkill\.exe$/i ParentBaseFileName=/powershell\.exe$/i
| regex("(?i)winrar\\.exe", field=CommandLine)
| regex("(?i)\\s/(F|IM)\\s", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name=taskkill.exe Processes.process="*winrar.exe*" Processes.parent_process_name=powershell.exe by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process Processes.parent_process Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where match(process, "(?i)/F") OR match(process, "(?i)/IM") | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name=taskkill.exe Processes.process="*winrar.exe*" Processes.parent_process_name=powershell.exe by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process Processes.parent_process Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where match(process, "(?i)/F") OR match(process, "(?i)/IM") | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
[LLM] PowerShower dropped to user Pictures folder as googleearth.ps1 Installation High
Hunts the documented PowerShower install path 'C:\Users\[username]\Pictures\googleearth.ps1' - an unusual location/name combination Cloud Atlas uses to hide its reconnaissance/Kerberoasting backdoor. Catches both the file-drop event and subsequent PowerShell execution. Rationale: Direct quote from article: 'PowerShower is dropped onto the system via the path C:\Users\[username]\Pictures\googleearth.ps1.' Filename + path combo is uniquely Cloud Atlas - Google Earth doesn't ship a .ps1 and Pictures isn't a normal script location. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0441/ • https://malpedia.caad.fkie.fraunhofer.de/details/win.powershower
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1547.001 T1564.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
union
(DeviceProcessEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
  | where ProcessCommandLine has "googleearth.ps1"
  | where ProcessCommandLine has @"\Pictures\" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has @"\Pictures\"
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, EventKind="Process", FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine),
(DeviceFileEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
  | where FileName =~ "googleearth.ps1"
  | where FolderPath has @"\Pictures\"
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, EventKind="FileDrop", FileName, ProcessCommandLine=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine)
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where CommandLine contains "googleearth.ps1"
| where CommandLine contains "Pictures"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName

[LLM] SAM/SECURITY registry hives copied from VSS shadow to Public\Documents as .pdf Actions on Objectives High
Hunts the PowerShower credential grabber: a Volume Shadow Copy is created and SAM/SECURITY hives are copied to C:\Users\Public\Documents\ disguised with a .pdf extension. The combination of HarddiskVolumeShadowCopy source paths, Public\Documents destination, and .pdf masquerade is unique to this article. Rationale: Article states verbatim: 'Copies the SAM (stores local user password hashes) and SECURITY system files from this shadow copy to C:\Users\Public\Documents\, disguising them as PDF files.' The triple constraint (Public\Documents + .pdf + SAM/SECURITY/shadow-copy reference) collapses FP rate to near zero. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003/002/ • https://malpedia.caad.fkie.fraunhofer.de/details/win.powershower
ATT&CKT1003.002 T1003.004 T1006 T1036.008
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has @"\Users\Public\Documents\" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has @"\Users\Public\Documents\"
| where ProcessCommandLine has ".pdf" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has ".pdf"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("SAM", "SECURITY", "HarddiskVolumeShadowCopy", "Win32_ShadowCopy", "vssadmin")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("SAM", "SECURITY", "HarddiskVolumeShadowCopy", "Win32_ShadowCopy", "vssadmin")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "cmd.exe", "wmic.exe", "fodhelper.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where CommandLine contains "Public\\Documents"
| where CommandLine contains ".pdf"
| where CommandLine has_any ("SAM", "SECURITY", "HarddiskVolumeShadowCopy", "Win32_ShadowCopy", "vssadmin")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
